subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Mayan Astronomy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Mayan Astronomy.

hook.text: The Maya tracked Venus with astonishing accuracy—their tables predicted its cycle to within two hours over 500 years.

buildup.text: They built observatories like El Caracol at Chichén Itzá, with windows aligned to Venus's extreme positions.

discovery.text: The Dresden Codex, a surviving Maya book, contains Venus tables used for both astronomy and warfare planning.

twist.text: Venus was linked to war. Maya rulers timed battles to Venus's appearance—celestial events dictated when to attack.

climax.text: Maya math used zero and base-20 counting. Their calendar system tracked cycles spanning millions of years.

punchline.text: Venus guided their wars. The sky shaped an empire's decisions.

quiz.question: How did the Maya use their astronomical observations of Venus?
options: They timed warfare and political events to Venus's appearances
They used Venus to navigate across the Atlantic Ocean
They predicted earthquakes based on Venus's position

details.summary: The Maya civilization developed sophisticated astronomical knowledge independently from the Old World. They tracked Venus's 584-day cycle with extraordinary precision, predicted eclipses, and created a calendar system accurate to within seconds per year.
details.whyItMatters: Mayan astronomy demonstrates that advanced astronomical knowledge developed independently across cultures. Their Venus tables and eclipse predictions rival or exceed Babylonian and Greek accuracy, achieved entirely without telescopes or Old World…
takeaways: The Maya tracked Venus's cycle with extraordinary precision
They predicted eclipses and created remarkably accurate calendars
Their astronomy developed independently from Old World traditions

faq.question: How accurate was the Maya calendar?
faq.answer: The Maya calculated the solar year as 365.2420 days — the actual value is 365.2422 days, an error of only 17 seconds per year. Their Venus cycle measurement of 583.92 days is accurate to within 2 hours over 481 years. This precision was achieved through centuries of careful naked-eye observation.

faq.question: What is the Dresden Codex?
faq.answer: A pre-Columbian Maya book containing detailed astronomical tables, including Venus cycle calculations, eclipse prediction tables, and Mars observations. It's one of only four surviving Maya books (Spanish colonizers destroyed thousands) and is the most complete record of Maya astronomical knowledge.
